Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State of U.P. and perused the record.
3. This Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 302 of 2020, (Criminal Case No. 2805 of 2021), under Sections 395, 412, 120-B IPC, P.S.
Arnia, District Bulandshahr during the pendency of trial.

1 3. Allegation against the applicant is that he along with other co accused persons are said to have looted away the motorcycle, mobile and Rs. 18,30,000/- of the informant.
4. It is submitted that in this case applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated by the police with ulterior motive.
There is no credible evidence to connect the applicant with the crime in question.
There is no independent witness of the incident.
The applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.

It is further submitted that the applicant was earlier granted anticipatory bail till submission of the charge sheet vide order dated 26.3.2021 passed in Criminal misc Anticipatory Bail Application No. 4661 of 2021.

entities.text: Criminal misc Anticipatory Bail Application No. 4661 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Now the charge sheet has been filed, hence the present anticipatory bail application after rejection of the anticipatory bail by the court below.

It is further submitted that the applicant has explained the criminal history of three cases; one relates to Section 363, 376 IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act, in which applicant has been acquitted by the court below; second case relates to Section 323, 504, 506,364, 511 IPC, in which final report has been submitted against the applicant and the third case relates to Gangster Act, in which he has been bailed out.
5.
Learned Additional Government Advocate, has opposed the prayer for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
It is further submitted that the alleged looted money has been recovered from the possession of the wife of the applicant from his house, therefore, no case for bail is made out.

6. In the light of above, looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties as mentioned above, taking into consideration the role assigned to the applicant as per prosecution case, gravity and nature of accusation, this Court is of the view that no case for exercising its discretionary power under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is made out in favour of applicant.
7. Accordingly, this application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is rejected.
